Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates marked dilation of the trachea and main bronchi (indicated by arrowheads), which is the pathognomonic radiological sign of Mounier-Kuhn syndrome (tracheobronchomegaly). This anatomical defect leads to ineffective mucociliary clearance, explaining the patient's history of recurrent lower respiratory infections and chronic productive cough.
